cards.explanation: The answer is two baskets of figs. Jeremiah, the prophet telling this story, says the LORD showed him "…two baskets of figs placed in front of the temple of the LORD." (Jeremiah 24:1) Not a pot, not a branch, just two baskets of fruit sitting right there. I've baked a lot of batches and I've never once had a vision about them, so I'm a little jealous, friends.

The answer is False. The other basket held "…very poor figs, so bad they could not be eaten." (Jeremiah 24:2) Nobody was going to nibble on those and say they weren't so bad. The text leaves no wiggle room, and neither do I, friends.

The answer is the exiles taken from Judah. The LORD says, "Like these good figs, so I regard as good the exiles from Judah…" (Jeremiah 24:5) These are the people Babylon carried away. You'd expect the ones who got hauled off to be the bad basket, right? The LORD flips that around, bakers.

The answer is True. The LORD says the exiles are those "…whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans." (Jeremiah 24:5) Chaldeans is another name for the people of Babylon. He says it plainly, friends, and He's still calling these exiles good.

The two words are build and plant. God says, "I will build them up and not tear them down…" (Jeremiah 24:6) I've been torn down and built back up myself, friends, and building is the better deal. Then He says, "I will plant them and not uproot them." (Jeremiah 24:6) Planting and not uprooting go together, like a seed that gets to stay in the ground.

The answer is that they will turn back to Him completely. God says, "They will be My people, and I will be their God, for they will return to Me with all their heart." (Jeremiah 24:7) The reason is right there in the verse, friends: they come back with all their heart. Not half, not most of the way. All of it.

The answer is those living in Egypt. God says He'll deal with "…Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem—those remaining in this land and those living in the land of Egypt." (Jeremiah 24:8) So the bad basket reaches past the borders, bakers. Some had gone down to Egypt, and they're counted too.

The word is scorn. God says He'll make them "…a disgrace and an object of scorn, ridicule, and cursing wherever I have banished them." (Jeremiah 24:9) This one is heavy, so I'll just say it plainly, friends. Scorn is the word in the verse.

The answer is True. God says, "And I will send against them sword and famine and plague, until they have perished from the land that I gave to them and their fathers." (Jeremiah 24:10) It's a heavy verse, friends, and I think it's okay to sit quiet with it for a second. That's what the text says.
